title: What's Happening with Your PPF and Other Small Savings Rates?
description: The Indian government reviews interest rates for popular small savings schemes like PPF every three months. The next announcement, setting rates for July-Sept.

faq.a: These are a collection of investment schemes offered by the Indian government to encourage savings among citizens, including popular options like Public Provident Fund (PPF), National Savings Certificates (NSC), Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS), and Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana.

faq.q: How often are these rates changed?
faq.a: The interest rates for small savings schemes are reviewed and announced by the government every three months, meaning they are updated quarterly.

faq.q: Will my old investments also get the new rate?
faq.a: Yes, for most small savings schemes like PPF, the new interest rate announced for the quarter applies to both new deposits made during that period and the existing balance in your account for that specific quarter.

faq.q: Where can I find the official announcement?
faq.a: The Ministry of Finance generally makes the announcement through official notifications. This information is then widely reported by reputable financial news outlets and published on government websites.

faq.q: Why do these rates matter if I don't use these schemes?
faq.a: Even if you don't directly invest in these schemes, their rates often reflect the broader interest rate environment in the Indian economy. This can indirectly influence rates on bank fixed deposits, home loans, and other investments, giving you a general idea of market trends.
